items.problem: The failure value of `create_test_match` does not cover the game transaction that saves the match record. The cell lists only the two input throws, and the failure handling of step 1 of `### match creation` sends `MATCH_FAILED` to participants, which this operation does not have because it has no connections. So when that transaction is `FAILED`, throwing and returning `FAILED` both fit the spec, and `dev` of `routing` (skills/server-core/modules/routing.md:74) passes either result to the test differently.

`matchmaker.helloTimeoutMs` and `matchmaker.frameReadTimeoutMs` (line 273) write no range, so skills/core/SKILL.md:133-134 allows 0. Line 209 measures both with `server-time.network_time_limit`, which throws when ms is less than 1 (skills/server-core/modules/server-time.md:39). Run path: a value of 0 passes the schema, then the call throws at connection accept or at a frame read, and no document sets what happens to that connection. `p2p-signaling.turnTimeoutMs` (skills/server-core/modules/p2p-signaling.md:124) and `push.sendTimeoutMs` (skills/server-core/modules/push.md:195) write `1 or more`. Direction: write `1 or more` on both keys.

`matchmaker.applyRetryMaxAttempts` writes no range, so 0 is allowed. Line 198 gives up when `attempts` reaches this value, and `attempts` is 1 after the first `FAILED`. Run path: with 0, an equality comparison never gives up, so the index is never marked and `expires_at` is never set (line 203), while a comparison with `≥` gives up at the first failure. Both implementations follow the text. `push.retryMaxAttempts` (skills/server-core/modules/push.md:197) and `storage.userChangeRetryMaxAttempts` (skills/server-core/modules/storage.md:365) write `1 or more`. Direction: write `1 or more` on this key.

Step 3 of the `MATCH_REQUEST` processing order waits for `run_rollback_transaction` (an async operation, skills/server-core/modules/storage.md:43), and step 4 puts the entry in the queue with no further condition. Lines 105 and 121 only remove a user who is already in the queue, and the user is not in it during step 3. No document sets the result of a connection close, `MATCH_CANCEL`, a second `MATCH_REQUEST` or `ROOM_CREATE` that arrives during step 3; line 137 sets this wait only for room members. Run path: the connection closes during step 3 and the entry of the closed connection still enters the queue and can become a match; or a second `MATCH_REQUEST` during step 3 gives two entries, which contradicts line 115. Direction: set the frame handling order per connection, and recheck the connection and the cancel state before step 4.

`ROOM_START` is `ROOM_BUSY` only when the room is `Matching`, and neither `ROOM_START` nor member rating resolution changes the status of an `Open` room; host `MATCH_REQUEST` (line 151) changes it to `Matching` only after resolution. Line 137 sets the result only when the members change during that wait. Run path: the host sends `ROOM_START` twice, and the second frame arrives while the first waits for `prepare_match_request`. Nothing in the text refuses it, so one implementation creates two matches with the same members and another drops the second frame. The same holds for `ROOM_START` followed by host `MATCH_REQUEST`, and for a second `ROOM_START` during match creation. Direction: set the result of a host frame that arrives during member rating resolution and match creation of that room.

Host `MATCH_CANCEL` changes the room to `Open` with no exception, while line 89 defines `Matching` as including a party entry that is becoming a match, line 144 keeps such a room `Matching` for `ROOM_LEAVE`, and line 153 changes it to `Open` only after `MATCH_FOUND` or `MATCH_FAILED`(`CREATE_FAILED`). Run path: the host sends `MATCH_CANCEL` after matching collected the party entry and before `MATCH_FOUND`. By line 152 the room is `Open` and the host can send `MATCH_REQUEST` or `ROOM_START` while the first match is being created; by lines 89 and 153 it stays `Matching`. Direction: state for `MATCH_CANCEL` the same exception that `ROOM_LEAVE` has.

`matchmaker.frameReadTimeoutMs` has no written range, so value 0 is allowed and a frame read reaches the throw of `network_time_limit` (skills/core/SKILL.md:134, skills/server-core/modules/matchmaker.md:209, skills/server-core/modules/server-time.md:39)

A connection that closes during match creation is not handled in the match session. Line 161 passes the connections of the participants to `open_match_session`, whose connection list must match `players` in count (skills/server-core/modules/p2p-signaling.md:29), so the closed connection is bound (p2p-signaling.md:62). `connection_closed` already ran while that connection was unbound and returned none (p2p-signaling.md:157), and line 162 only writes `DISCONNECTED` to the record. Run path: a participant closes between step 1 and step 2. The other participants get no `PEER_LEFT`, a `PEER_SIGNAL` to that index passes the bound check and goes to a closed connection, and the session is not deleted as one without a bound connection until `expires_at` (p2p-signaling.md:64). When the user reconnected during creation, no document sets whether the new connection replaces the old one in the list, so `MATCH_FOUND` goes to the closed connection and the new connection does not learn the `match_id`. Direction: set the connection used for a participant whose connection closed or was replaced during creation, and the `PEER_LEFT` the others get.

The close handling removes "that user" from the queue and the room, and a queue entry member and a room member are user IDs (lines 114, 133), not connections. Line 104 closes the previous connection when a new connection is authenticated, and no document sets whether the close handling of the previous connection finishes before frames of the new connection are handled. Run path: connection B of the user is authenticated, B sends `MATCH_REQUEST` or `ROOM_CREATE`, and then the close of previous connection A is handled. An implementation that handles the close on the socket close event removes the entry or room membership that B just made, and one that handles it during the authentication of B keeps it. Direction: run the close handling of the previous connection synchronously at the authentication of the new connection, or key the removal by connection.

Each participant change is written by its own async game transaction, and no document sets their order for one match. The error row on line 244 refuses a retry because "a retried `DISCONNECTED` could be written after a later `REJOINED`", but a first attempt has the same order problem on PostgreSQL, where transactions run on several connections and each waits for its own connection and row lock (skills/server-core/modules/storage.md:297). Run path: a `DISCONNECTED` write waits while the `REJOINED` write of the same index commits, then writes `disconnected_at` as non-zero for a participant who is connected. Line 186 then does not wait for that participant's report in a `ServerReplay` judgement, so the result can differ from the one with the writes in event order. Direction: set that the participant changes of one match are written one at a time in the order they happened.

The counting window of the per-IP limits `matchmaker.preAuthAcceptsPerSecond` and `matchmaker.preAuthFramesPerSecond` is not set. Line 209 says only "per-second counts" for them while it uses "the last 1000 ms" for the user frame count on line 210, and line 213 takes only the IP judgement from `routing`, whose counters use the minute window (skills/server-core/modules/routing.md:168). Run path: with a limit of 10, 10 accepts at `clock_now` 999 and 10 accepts at `clock_now` 1001 all pass with a fixed window of `server-time.get_window_start`, and the second 10 get HTTP 429 with the last 1000 ms. Direction: name one window for both limits, and add a test at its boundary.

The test item says "the index that left has `left_at` and `reported_at` 0", which reads as `left_at` 0 for a participant who did `MATCH_LEAVE`, contrary to line 232 (`left_at` is 0 only when none); the parallel clause "the remaining index has `reported_at` and `result`" suggests the intent is `left_at` not 0 and `reported_at` 0, so the judgement criterion of that item differs per reader
